items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: Dizzy commissioned me to write a three-movement suite... I went with Dizzy... Dizzy's pianist

ctx.x: So there’s pros and cons to both I guess.

Well now I’m used to the computer, but when I did the pencil I would go into — the best way to describe it — a music trance. And I’d be writing like that. Because I remember Dizzy commissioned me to write a three-movement suite. It was originally for the London Philharmonic with him. I wrote from ten in the morning to four AM, seven days a week for seven weeks. And I swear to God the time went by like, holy, it’s that late already, and I’d get a few hours sleep. And when I got finished I had a gig in Fort…

“Well that’s ‘cause where your head was at when you were writing that piece of music.” But I was in a music trance if you can understand, like you’re in a place. And the music is unfolding in your ear and you’re just writing it down like you’re taking dictation you know.
